# Fixed: Link extra files imported with a track to its track file

Part of the [custom Lidarr image](https://github.com/chodeus/Lidarr/tree/custom) (`ghcr.io/chodeus/lidarr:custom`), which merges this branch into `develop`. It is stacked on [`fix/replace-import-rollback`](https://github.com/chodeus/Lidarr/tree/fix/replace-import-rollback), which reworks the same import loop, and merges after it.

With Import Extra Files on, a download's lyrics (`.lrc`, `.txt`) and other extra files are imported beside each track. Develop imports them inside the track loop of `ImportApprovedTracks`, before `AddMany` saves the new track files, so each track file still has id 0 and every extra file row is stored with `TrackFileId` 0. Renaming the tracks then leaves those extra files behind under the old names, and deleting or upgrading the track leaves them in the album folder. The artist scan keeps such a row as long as its file is on disk.

- Extra files are imported after `AddMany` (and after each album's backed-up files are settled), so each row links to its track file. An extra file that fails to import logs a warning; the track still counts as imported. Before, the failure marked the already-moved track "Failed to import track".
- Two housekeeping tasks, ported from Sonarr's `CleanupOrphanedExtraFiles` and `CleanupOrphanedSubtitleFiles`, delete `ExtraFiles` and `LyricFiles` rows whose artist or track file is gone, as `CleanupOrphanedMetadataFiles` does for `MetadataFiles`. A row stored with `TrackFileId` 0 is linked to the track file in its folder whose name, followed by a dot, starts the file's name (the longest such name, so `Mr. Blue Sky.lrc` goes to `Mr. Blue Sky.flac`, not `Mr.flac`; case counts as it does in Lidarr's path comparison, so only on Windows does `song.lrc` go to `Song.flac`): an extra file is named after its track file when it's imported. A row that no track file matches, because its track was renamed since, or that two track files match equally (`Song.lrc` beside `Song.flac` and `Song.wav`), keeps `TrackFileId` 0 as before. Each artist's links are written in one transaction. Sonarr deletes such rows; here the artist scan would then pick a file up again only if it could parse the name to a track.

Linking every imported extra file makes the code that removes a track file's extras reach all of them, where before it reached only those the artist scan had linked. Three of its callers removed extras they shouldn't, and one that should didn't:
- Removing a root folder in settings drops only Lidarr's rows now, as a cleanup with no history entry. Before, it counted as deleting each track file, so the extras beside the files went to the recycle bin (or were deleted, with no recycle bin set) while the audio stayed.
- A file imported again at the same path (a rescan after a tagger changed it, or after a release switch unlinked its tracks) keeps its extras: their rows move to the file's new row once it's saved, and to its album if it now belongs to another. Before, they were recycled. If the new rows can't be saved, the file's previous row comes back, linked to its tracks, and its extras follow it; before, its tracks had no file until a rescan. A row that comes back but can't be linked to its tracks is removed again, so a rescan imports the file. Whenever the row can't be put back, its extras are left unlinked, and housekeeping links them by name to the row the rescan gives the file.
- A disk scan that finds a track file gone (it may only have been renamed outside Lidarr, by a tagger say) drops only its rows: the lyrics, cue sheets and logs that came with the album stay on disk beside it. Before, they went to the recycle bin, which empties itself after 7 days by default. Deleting a track file in Lidarr still recycles its extras with it.
- Deleting an album with its files recycles the extras of the track files it deletes, and the album's own, lyrics and metadata files included; a track file it leaves (one on an unmonitored release) keeps its extras. A row stored with `TrackFileId` 0 goes with the album; its file goes to the recycle bin only when the one track file it's named after, by the rule housekeeping links by, is being deleted. One whose name fits a file the album keeps just as well stays on disk. Each file is recycled on its own, so one that can't be stays on disk with a warning and the rest still go. Before, they stayed behind and kept the album folder from being removed as empty.

`ExtraService` keeps develop's constructor for plugins (a file imported again then loses its extras' links, as in develop), and so do `ExtraFileService` and the lyric, metadata and other extra file services (an album deleted with its files then leaves its unlinked extras on disk). `IExtraService.RelinkTrackFile` has a default body. Each kind of extra file is relinked on its own, so one that fails leaves the others linked. The album handler is synchronous, so the extras are gone before `MediaFileDeletionService` looks for the album folder to be empty. Housekeeping reads only the track files under the artist folders of unlinked rows, and now runs on its own, as `fix/log-cleansing-housekeeping-backups` also makes it, so the command queue never runs it while an import has a file's old row deleted and its extras not yet moved.

Tests: extra files imported with a track over the real services and test database (both rows linked to the new track file; failed before the change with `TrackFileId` 0); an extra file import that throws (the track still imports, with a warning); each housekeeping rule for both tables, including a row that must stay; relinking by name (the dot after the track's name, the longest name, case, the album, and a row nothing matches). Through the real media file, deletion and extra file services: a removed root folder keeps the extras on disk; so does a scan after the audio was renamed outside Lidarr; a user's track file deletion recycles them; an album deleted with its files recycles them, and one deleted without keeps them; a file imported again, changed or after a release switch, keeps its extras linked to its new row; when the save fails, its previous row comes back with its track and extras, only once the new row on its path is gone, and is removed again if its tracks can't be linked; a row that can't be put back leaves its extras unlinked; a previous row that can't be deleted keeps its extras' links; the container resolves all three extra file services as relinkers, with the media file service, and hands them to `ExtraService`; built with develop's constructor, an extra file service drops an unlinked row on album deletion and leaves its file; one relinker that throws leaves the next to run; the queue holds housekeeping back while an import runs; the album handler is synchronous, recycles only the deleted track files' extras and the album's own, an unlinked row's file only when it's named after a deleted track file beside it and not as well after one the album keeps, and goes on past a file it can't recycle; relinking moves the album too; a tie between two track files stays unlinked. Each was broken on purpose and caught by a test.
